compactMembership.notes: Arkansas's reciprocity operates via listed state-by-state reciprocal agreements (17 CAR 210-509 plus the Board's own Reciprocal Agreements roster) under which an applicant must still be issued a distinct Arkansas license — not a single multistate license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact, e.g. the Nurse Licensure Compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating this reciprocal-agreement mechanism with a compact, matching the same reasoning already applied to Colorado's NERA-based reciprocity in colorado-master.json.

reciprocityRules.value: Arkansas recognizes a separate, smaller Master Reciprocal Agreement list of only 4 states: Iowa, North Dakota, Oregon, and Texas — distinct from the 17-state Journeyman Reciprocal Agreement list. Critically, a master license from any of the OTHER 15 states on the Journeyman list (including Iowa and Texas, which appear on both lists) reciprocates into Arkansas as a JOURNEYMAN license only, not a master license. Only Oregon and North Dakota have a genuine master-to-master reciprocal agreement with Arkansas: a master license from those two states reciprocates directly into an Arkansas master license. As with the journeyman list, only an original (non-reciprocated) out-of-state license qualifies — a license itself obtained by reciprocity in the issuing state cannot be re-reciprocated into Arkansas.

reciprocityRules.notes: 17 CAR 210-404(e)(2) codifies explicit reciprocity conditions (held 1 year, tested, good standing) for JOURNEYMAN applicants specifically — see arkansas-journeyman.json; the administrative rules text does not restate an equivalent explicit condition for master-tier reciprocity. The master-tier mechanics recorded here (the 4-state list and the Oregon/North Dakota master-to-master exception) come only from the Board's own Reciprocal Agreements page (retrieved 2026-09-04 via direct browser access, the page being Cloudflare-protected against automated fetch), not the codified rules. Whether the journeyman-tier's 1-year/tested/good-standing conditions also apply to master reciprocity is NOT confirmed and is not assumed here.

endorsementRules.notes: Arkansas's own materials describe this mechanism as a 'Reciprocal Agreement' specifically (17 CAR 210-509; Board's Reciprocal Agreements page) — no separate 'endorsement' pathway or terminology was identified, matching the same finding already recorded for Colorado's NERA-based reciprocity in colorado-master.json.

requiredExams.value: A written examination ($80 fee) is required for standard/apprenticeship-path master licensure, per 17 CAR 210-403(a),(c). No explicit examination exemption is stated for master reciprocity applicants anywhere in the rules text — the master qualification section (210-404(d)) does not even include a dedicated reciprocity subsection, unlike journeyman's 210-404(e)(2) — so whether reciprocal master applicants must sit Arkansas's exam is unconfirmed and inferred only from the rule's general structure.

requiredExams.notes: Lower confidence than the equivalent journeyman field: master's qualification section (210-404(d)) has no dedicated reciprocity subsection at all (journeyman's 210-404(e)(2) does), so this is inferred purely from the rule's general structure, not from any master-specific text. Should be confirmed directly with the Board before being treated as certain.

requiredExperience.value: Arkansas's rules do not codify a master-tier-specific reciprocity experience or testing condition (unlike the explicit condition set for journeyman reciprocity under 17 CAR 210-404(e)(2) — see arkansas-journeyman.json). For ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) Arkansas master licensure: a degree in electrical engineering plus 2 years of construction-related experience; OR 6 years of construction industry experience (both residential and commercial) including 2 years as a licensed journeyman electrician; OR a board-approved equivalent combination of training and experience (17 CAR 210-404(d)).

requiredEducation.notes: No standalone formal-education requirement distinct from the pathways already captured in requiredExperience was identified — matching the same scope decision already made in colorado-master.json.

requiredDocuments.notes: Unlike journeyman reciprocity (17 CAR 210-404(e)(2), which explicitly requires sister-state certification of license status/duration/testing — see arkansas-journeyman.json), the rules text contains no equivalent explicit documentation requirement for master-tier reciprocity specifically. Not assumed to be identical to the journeyman requirement without confirmation.

endorsementFeeUsd.notes: Arkansas's rules do not define a distinct 'endorsement' or 'reciprocity issuance' fee separate from the standard $80 master examination fee (17 CAR 210-403(c)) — and whether reciprocal applicants must even pay that exam fee is itself unconfirmed (see requiredExams). Not recorded here to avoid conflating the general exam fee with a reciprocity-specific fee, matching Colorado's own explicit 'NOT independently confirmed' treatment of this field in colorado-master.json.
